messages:
Alex Martinez: Dropping DevEx feedback from community + a couple SE calls re: Usage Insights naming.

Main confusion: we keep saying “route” but devs think “routing policy” / “traffic routing” not “API endpoint”. People also mix up route vs method vs full URL.

Suggestion: UI label should bias toward “Endpoint” and show normalized route path as the value.

Examples:
- “Endpoint” column value: `POST /v1/chat/completions` (or just `/v1/chat/completions` if we don’t want method)
- Tooltip: “Endpoint is the normalized HTTP path used for grouping. Dynamic IDs are replaced with placeholders.”

Also: docs should explicitly say route == endpoint path pattern. Otherwise we’ll keep getting “why are my endpoints missing?” type reports.

Elliot Price: +1. In docs we can lead with “Endpoint (normalized route)” the first time, then stick to “Endpoint” afterwards.

Can we confirm what console is planning to label it as? I’m about to draft the glossary/tooltips.

Marissa Cole: We used “Route” in early mocks because backend uses route normalization, but I agree it’s not the best term externally.

Design currently has “Route” in filter chips + table header. We can change to “Endpoint” if we’re aligned.

Tessa Morgan: Yeah, “Route” reads internal. For most users “endpoint” is the mental model.

Proposal:
- Table header: “Endpoint”
- Filter label: “Endpoint”
- Value formatting: show `/v1/...` (maybe also method as pill?)
- Tooltip copy mentions “normalized route pattern” for accuracy

Alicia Perez: If we show method too, it could add clutter. Most Redwood API routes are unique even without it.

Could do:
- Primary text: `/v1/chat/completions`
- Secondary (muted) text in row expand: “HTTP method: POST”

Alex Martinez: Works. Most devs just need “which endpoint is costing me”. If we bury method that’s fine.

One more confusion: “route” vs “model” in the same sentence. People read “route/model breakdown” as “request routing by model”.

Maybe in copy: “Cost by endpoint and model” instead of “route + model”.

Paula Mendes: Noted. PRD text can shift to “endpoint + model” in user-facing areas.

We should keep “route” in the technical docs/ADR only.

Wei Chen: For help center article/tooltips, I can add a short glossary box:
- Endpoint: API path used for grouping (normalized)
- Normalization: replaces dynamic segments with placeholders
- Example: `/v1/files/123` → `/v1/files/{file_id}`

Also clarify the difference between “Endpoint” and “Project”/“Environment” filters.

Elliot Price: Love it. Also call out OpenAI-compat endpoints explicitly:
- `/v1/chat/completions`
- `/v1/completions`
- `/v1/embeddings`

We keep getting “I’m using the OpenAI SDK, where do I find those?”

Marissa Cole: Good call. We can add a tooltip line like “Includes OpenAI-compatible endpoints when enabled”.

Dylan Brooks: Heads up: backend canonical route keys don’t include HTTP method today. Adding method as a first-class dimension would be extra work and increases cardinality.

So I’d prefer we display path-only.

Alex Martinez: Fine by DevEx. Just don’t call it “Route” :)

Markus Klein: From SE side: customers keep asking “why do I see `/v1/chat/completions/{id}`?” They assume they’re calling it wrong.

If we normalize, the UI should *show* it’s normalized, otherwise it looks like a weird literal URL.

Maybe we add an icon + tooltip: “Grouped by normalized endpoint”.

Tessa Morgan: Agree. We can add info icon next to header. Tooltip copy:
“Endpoints are normalized for reporting. Dynamic path segments (IDs) are replaced with placeholders so totals don’t split across many values.”

Wei Chen: Also we should be careful with placeholder formatting. `{file_id}` is readable, but some docs prefer `:file_id`.

Do we have a standard?

Dylan Brooks: In route normalization lib draft we were leaning `{param}`. It’s consistent with other Redwood docs + OpenAPI-ish.

Elliot Price: Great, I’ll match `{param}` in docs.

Alex Martinez: Another terminology nit: “tokens in/out” vs “prompt/completion tokens”. Many folks coming from OpenAI expect prompt/completion.

Could we label in tooltips:
- “Tokens in (prompt)”
- “Tokens out (completion)”

And keep the short label in the table.

Marissa Cole: That’s reasonable. We can keep table columns “Tokens in” / “Tokens out” and add tooltip subtitle mapping.

Alicia Perez: I’ll add to UX spec: tooltip text should include parenthetical mapping.

Wei Chen: I’ll include the mapping in the help article too + mention streaming overhead & retries:
- Streaming overhead: extra request/connection overhead may increase cost slightly (if applicable)
- Retries: re-attempted requests counted in usage; can inflate spend

Alex Martinez: One more: “cache hit rate” explanation. People interpret as CDN cache. Should say “prefix/KV cache” and link to Optimize docs.

Elliot Price: Yep. Tooltip:
“Cache hit rate measures reuse of prefix/KV cache in the inference runtime (not HTTP caching). Higher hit rate reduces billed tokens / compute.”

(We’ll need to ensure it’s true to billing semantics, but at least clarify what cache refers to.)

Marissa Cole: Please add “not HTTP caching” — we’ve seen that confusion.

Paula Mendes: Action items:
- Design: swap “Route” → “Endpoint” across UI (table + filters) and add header tooltip about normalization
- Docs: glossary + examples + OpenAI-compat callout; map tokens in/out to prompt/completion
- DevEx: provide final tooltip copy suggestions + links to Optimize docs

Alex Martinez: I’ll drop proposed tooltip strings in the doc draft and tag @Elliot Price / @Wei Chen.

:thumbsup: (reactions from Marissa Cole, Tessa Morgan)

Wei Chen: Cool. Also, where should the docs live? Existing console docs section under “Usage & Billing” or new “Usage Insights” page?

Elliot Price: New “Usage Insights” page under Console → Usage/Cost. We can cross-link from Billing FAQ.

Marissa Cole: Works. For in-console, we can add “Learn more” link in the tooltip popover to that page.

Alex Martinez: Great. That should reduce tickets like “what is route” / “why is this endpoint weird”.
